headline: Phase E of the owner-approved plan (docs/status/handoff/NEXT-SESSION.md): the leftovers sweep, real problems first, polish batched. Input: the 102 items of /tmp/frbench/handoffs.json 'later', each checked against claude/nifty-knuth-f9udt0 at f64d7e9 (the 'triage' array: 13 real, 44 polish, 21 already fixed, 9 owned by phase C, 9 duplicates, 6 out of scope; reviewed 2026-11-02: #75/#83 moved from phase C to 'screens'). Sources: the fix waves' reports, the wave 3 reviews, the live reports (docs/status/handoff/round-2026-11-01/live-reports/live1 to live4). Phase C's four areas (/tmp/frbench/phaseC.json) own their items and are not repeated here. Phase E starts only after phase C is merged: its areas touch files phase C changes (person-questions.ts, request-answers.ts, runner.ts, executor.ts, StartSessionDialog.tsx, TaskDrawer.tsx, task-words.ts, role-player.ts, fake-daemon.ts); each fixer rebases its worktree on the branch after that merge. Same pipeline as phase C: failing test first at the boundary the person uses, the full suite at every stage, an independent reviewer who walks the acceptance on the bench, one merge at a time. Wave 7 (2026-11-02): the owner's decisions of 2026-11-02 and the planned 'cost' and 'polish', as fourteen areas in six groups appended to areas and parallel_groups (the old planned group ['cost', 'polish'] is replaced by them); the wave 7 spec alone is /tmp/frbench/phaseE7.json and its live check /tmp/frbench/phaseE7-live.md; the file before wave 7 is /tmp/frbench/phaseE.before-wave7.json. | Wave 13 (base ce13bb1): polish-words, polish-screens, and the logic leftovers of waves 12/14 in leftovers7-tailmerge and leftovers7-tailrun.

areas.title: Chat and Inbox answers do what the person said: one card per question, no task closed by a word its card does not offer, a start that is true, a chat that reads real docs and adds tasks with real titles
problems: [real, major] later #3: 'A free-text 'go ahead' on a planned person card closes the task although the card offers no Go ahead without.' Still so on f64d7e9: personQuestionsAnswer (packages/runtime/src/wiring/request-answers.ts:206) reads a typed 'go ahead' as {kind: 'without'} for every questions card; person-questions.ts:652-668 then walks a planned card's task (on_answer 'done') through CLOSE_PATH with no answers and resumeWork starts what waited on it. The planned card ('"X" needs your answers', request-words.ts:287-311) offers only the form and Cancel task. A chat 'go ahead' (request_answer tool), the phone or the web approvals close e.g. 'Owner supplies the bakery's real content' empty, and the coder after it builds on nothing: live2 #3's symptom by another road.

[real, minor] later #1: 'Chat 'yes' on a medium-risk card may still file the executor's pending yes/no card beside the original (needs_yes path).' Still so: the executor's gate (packages/commands/src/executor.ts:345-357) short-circuits request.answer only for needs_device ('Answer it on its card in the Inbox…', wave 2). request.answer takes the card's own risk (commands/request.ts:42); the plan card (session/intake.ts:1208), the failed-run card (session/runner.ts:1058) and the review/findings cards (session/findings.ts:304, :374) are medium, so 'approve the plan' or 'try it again' in chat gets needs_yes and createPending (executor.ts:362-395) inserts a second Inbox request (kind approval, yes/no) about the first. Two cards for one question (design §3.8; U-029).

[real, minor] later #34 (live2 part 3 C2) with #25 (live2 #8): 'chat-added task title keeps 'to …', no criteria, 'Agent's choice''; 'title = raw sentence cut at 80 chars'. Live: 'Added "to write a README that explains…"'; 'make a 404.html 'page not found' page in the same style as the others, with a l…'. matchAddTask (packages/commands/src/intent.ts:601-617) takes the rest of the line as title (sliced at 120) and as outcome; Make this a task (:634-636) the same. areas.fix_scope: 1. A typed answer to a card is read against the card's own choices: on a planned person card 'go ahead' is not Go ahead without; it is refused in words ('This card needs your answers: type them, or Cancel task') and the card stays open; the chat's request_answer gets the same refusal and says it. The specialist card keeps Go ahead without. 2. request.answer from chat or voice never files a second card: either the chat's own read-back and yes confirm it (nothing goes to the Inbox), or it is refused like needs_device with 'Answer it on its card in the Inbox'. Decide by design §3.8/§3.9, say which in the commit, test the plan card ('approve the plan') and a failed-task card ('try it again') with the option strings the Inbox shows. 3. matchAddTask/matchTask: drop a leading 'to', 'please', 'can you'; a title is cut at a word under 80 characters and the full line stays the outcome; the read-back shows the title. With a model available, a line that is more than a title goes to the model's task_create tool (title, outcome, criteria); the parser stays for installs without a model (U-047). 4. Doc search skips scaffold sections (export the placeholders from memory/src/docs.ts and test both sides). 5. The chat's session.start waits like POST /sessions (session.started, the run's error, or the same timeout), links the session, and says a run that failed before its session began as the failure. 6. Polish 6-11 above; #15 is a design-doc sentence only.

areas.acceptance: Fresh bench (--provider bench --env FORERUNNER_BENCH_PERSON=1). The stand-in chat calls a command tool when told 'tool: <name> {json}' (testenv/src/bench/role-player.ts:812-833); the card's short reference is in the chat call's context (model-calls.jsonl) or GET /inbox. (a) Approve and start the plan; in Chat send 'tool: request_answer {"request": "<ref>", "answer": "go ahead"}' for the person task's card, and POST /requests/<id>/answer with the text 'go ahead' as the phone and the web approvals do: the card stays in Needs you, the reply says it needs answers or Cancel task, the task still reads 'Needs your answer'; answer through the form: it closes and the next task's brief (model-calls.jsonl) carries the answers. (b) Before approving, answer the plan card from chat (tool: request_answer with 'Approve and start'): the Inbox holds exactly one card about the plan (no 'approval' card), and after the chat's yes (or the refusal, per the decision) the plan is approved from its own card; same with a failed task (--env FORERUNNER_BENCH_FAIL=<title> FORERUNNER_BENCH_FAIL_TIMES=always) and answer its card from chat with 'Try again'. (c) With --provider none (the parser's path), chat 'Add a task to write a README that explains how to open the page': Tasks shows a title without 'to', under 80 characters, cut at a word. With --provider bench the same line must still add that task: if the fix sends longer lines to the model's task_create tool, the stand-in chat does that too (ask 'bench', which owns role-player.ts, in notes_for_other_areas) and the model path is confirmed live by a helper after the merge. (d) On a fresh small project chat 'what is next?': the chat call in model-calls.jsonl contains neither 'To be written' nor '- first task'. (e) Chat 'start a session': the reply links the running session. (f) Failing tests first; unit, real-daemon and restart cases; the full suite (pnpm check, test:integration, test:e2e, UI vitest, Playwright).
depends_on: phase C merged (continuity and verification change request-answers.ts, person-questions.ts and runner.ts)

(packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:572); for a data-analyst or science-evaluator whose deliverable is a report file, 'the report' reads as that file; nothing says scratch notes stay out of the project.

Decide in an ADR: the reviewer's findings are its report and Forerunner writes the file the task names, or the planner never gives a reviewer a 'write a file' outcome (validation rule 6). Do not pretend run_command is read-only.

areas.title: Work a person will use is tried in its own environment, whatever it is: a CLI is run, an API is called, a page is opened, inside the task's sandbox (the container when Docker is ready, always for a full review); the project's own tests run whatever the language; Chromium keeps its own sandbox
problems: [major] C-1: A CLI or an API a task builds is never tried, and nothing is tried in the task's own environment: only pages are tried, by a headless Chromium on the host with the network off, also for full-review work and on a PC where Docker is ready (where the task itself ran in the container, ADR 0101). The owner's decision (3) says work a person will use (a page, an app, a CLI, an API) is started in its own environment (the Docker sandbox on the owner's PC) and used as a person would.

[minor] C-3: The project's own tests run only when they are package.json scripts: a Python, Rust or Go project's tests (pytest, cargo test, go test) are never run by the review, and the review does not even say so ('See what was checked' lists nothing as not run), although the owner's decision (1) says the project's build, lint and tests always run for a code task.

[minor] C-17: The page try launches Chromium on the host with Playwright's default chromiumSandbox: false (--no-sandbox) and opens model-written pages with it at every level, full-review tasks' pages too, while ADR 0101 runs full-review work only in the container.
[minor] L-4: A retry brief turns every critic note into an instruction, including notes the critic called unrelated or not asked for, so the retry edits code outside its task.
[minor] L-5: A worker can redefine the project's test script in the same change, and the runtime then runs the worker's version as the project's check.

[minor] R-1: The page try can leave a headless Chromium running: chromium.launch() runs before serveFolder()/mkdirSync() and outside the try/finally, so a throw from either leaves the browser process alive on the person's PC.

A merge conflict between dependencies is a card for the person, never a silent drop.

areas.title: Merging is safe before either mode ships (part 1): a durable merge record pins the reviewed version, a waiting merge is kept and retried with no session through one gated entry, merges are merge commits only, the branch's rules are read first, and the merge step never replays merged-in work
problems: [blocker] The merge step replays a branch that carries another task's work. When main moved it rebases the PR branch (packages/runtime/src/loop/merge.ts:243 `git.rebaseOnto(base)`) and force-pushes it (:252). A dependent task's branch is built by merging its dependencies' unmerged branches in (packages/capabilities/src/githost/pr-executor.ts:322-349, DEPS_BASE_REF :129; its own comment :323-324: 'a rebase would copy that work into the branch as new commits'). The rebase copies the dependency's commits: its own commits never reach main, GitHub never marks its PR merged, and merging it later is an add/add conflict (research challenge's local run; /tmp/frbench/owner-q/gitexp). The PR executor's own syncs (execute()'s post-run sync and continueResolved) are 'dependent-branches''s.

[blocker] The reviewed version is not saved. ReviewedPrMerge.mergeReviewed takes 'the reviewed commit' to be the task worktree's HEAD when it runs (merge.ts:376-381); its own rebase moves that HEAD and force-pushes (merge.ts:240-256). A retry after a rebase, or after a crash in the middle of one, would merge a commit the critic never saw.

[blocker] A waiting merge is lost. A merge whose checks still run after DEFAULT_CHECKS_WAIT_MS (merge.ts:54, :305-312) files a card and writes only the task's reason text (merge.ts:524-527); nothing retries it when the checks turn green (the watcher only starts a session on an all-green head, githost-watcher.ts:22-40), and nothing is kept when the PC sleeps or the app closes between the critic's accept and the merge (runner.ts:1888-1903 calls the merge inline; there is no durable marker). 'unverified' and 'not_allowed' file no card at all (merge.ts ASKS_HUMAN :590-596).

[major] A retry outside a session has no authority of its own: mergeReviewed derives its token from the session's token (merge.ts:395-402 `tokens.derive(req.token, ...)`) and caps its wait with the session's deadline (:405-418), so a retry from the watcher or at the daemon's start would have neither; and a record kept 'per install' must say whose it is, because packages/state can be the shared Postgres store (packages/state/src/store.ts:9, :43 'postgres://').

[major] Squash is the default: GitHubHost.mergePullRequest sends merge_method 'squash' unless told otherwise (packages/capabilities/src/githost/github.ts:425) and the merge step never says (merge.ts:315-318, input built at :427 without method); the in-memory host ignores the method (memory.ts:203-225). The owner merged forerunner-sandbox #4 with a merge commit.

[major] Nothing reads the branch's rules: the merge uses the plain endpoint (github.ts:418-439). GitHub does not let a PR's author (Forerunner opens PRs with the person's own token) approve it; admins are exempt from classic branch protection by default; and merging a dependent PR marks its dependency merged 'even when branch protection rules were not satisfied' (GitHub docs, about pull request merges). An automatic merge, or an admin token, can go around the person's own rules.

Each task's agent keeps committing on its own branch. (this area builds the safe merge step under both modes: the record, the retry, merge commits only and the rules check; the modes and the button are 'merge-in-app''s)
root_causes: merge.ts mergeChecked (:191-338) always rebases and force-pushes a moved base (:240-256), whatever the branch holds, although a merge commit needs neither; pr-executor.ts keeps a merged-in branch current by merging (mergeMoved :530-549), but the merge step does not know that.
merge.ts reads the reviewed commit from the worktree at merge time (:376-381); the critic's accept writes no commit anywhere.

There is no durable merge state: MergeOutcome lives in the session's memory and the task's reason text (merge.ts:505-534); packages/state has no merge record, and the session waits up to 10 minutes inline (merge.ts:54, the polling loop :263-312) as the only chance; the token and the wait both come from the session (merge.ts:395-418).
github.ts:425 defaults to 'squash'; merge.ts passes no method; GitHost (types.ts:209-260) has no way to read a branch's rules, allow_merge_commit or a merged PR's merge commit.
areas.fix_scope: Engine only, no screen: the PR executor's sync paths, the dependent rebuilds and the watcher's merged/closed reporting are 'dependent-branches''s; the modes, the gate's mode check and the button are 'merge-in-app''s. (1) The record: a durable merge record per task in packages/state (one migration, tested on SQLite and on Postgres: migrations.integration.test.ts and postgres.integration.test.ts): task_id, project_id, agent_id (the install's own agent, which owns the record), PR number and URL, reviewed_head_sha, own_change_id (the patch id of the task's own change: the diff from DEPS_BASE_REF when the worktree has it, else from the merge base), state waiting_checks | queued | merging | merged | left_to_you, approval (none | mode | person, and who), merge_sha, method, attempts, sentence, updated_at. ReviewedPrMerge.mergeReviewed writes it first, on its first call after an accept, before any autonomy or mode check and in every mode and level (the worktree's HEAD is then the reviewed commit, before any rebase); from then on every merge uses the record's sha, never the worktree's HEAD. A task with no record (accepted before this change, or a crash before the record) is never merged unattended; 'merge-in-app''s click merges its current head and says so. (2) No replay in the merge step: mergeChecked never rebases and never force-pushes (today it rebases and force-pushes a moved base, merge.ts:240-256). When main moved, the PR is merged as it is with a merge commit (GitHub combines them; nothing is copied), unless an update is needed: a branch rule requires the branch to be up to date, or 'merge-in-app''s automatic mode needs the repository's checks on the combined result; then main is merged into the branch (git.mergeFrom origin/<base>, a merge commit and a normal push) when that merges cleanly, else the record goes to left_to_you with one sentence. After main was merged in, the record's reviewed version moves to the new head only when the task's own change is unchanged (own_change_id), else left_to_you with one sentence. Two helpers exported from packages/capabilities/src/githost (git.ts or a new branch-rules.ts): holdsMergedWork(git, base) (DEPS_BASE_REF in the worktree, or merge commits since the base: git.hasMergesSince) and ownChangeId(git, base); 'dependent-branches' uses the same two in the PR executor, which this area does not change. (3) One gated entry, persisted and retried: mergeRecorded(record, authority) is the only way anything merges a task PR (the session's accept, the watcher's retry, the resume at the daemon's start, and later 'merge-in-app''s click), and it asks one gate first, mayMerge(project, record, authority); in this area the gate's body is today's rule (unattended only at autonomy level 3; otherwise the person's approval), re-reading the project's level at every call; 'merge-in-app' replaces only the body with the merge mode, so no path can merge around it. A merge that waits (checks running, the session ending, sleep, a crash, the app closing) keeps its record. A retry never waits inline: a new pass in the watcher's poll (retryWaitingMerges, called from poll()) reads each waiting record's PR once and merges when its checks are green on the record's sha; the daemon's start resumes records left in 'merging' (merged on the host: mark merged; open: back to waiting). A retry or resume runs with no session: it issues its own narrow token (merge_pr only, that worktree, budget 0, a short expiry: tokens.issue, never tokens.derive from a session token) and goes through the hooks' beforeToolCall and its audit row unchanged. The watcher retries only the records of its own agent_id. A merge left to the person always carries one sentence on the record (no silent not_allowed or unverified: ASKS_HUMAN and STEPS, merge.ts:590-596). (4) Merge commits only: every merge Forerunner makes sends merge_method 'merge' pinned to the record's sha (merge.ts:315-318 passes it; github.ts:425's default becomes 'merge'); getRepo reads allow_merge_commit (github.ts:293-316); a repository that does not allow merge commits is never merged by Forerunner, with one sentence; the in-memory and testenv hosts honour the method (a merge commit has two parents; squash and rebase as GitHub makes them) and report merge_commit_sha. (5) The rules: before any merge, read the branch's rules (GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rules/branches/{b}, and the classic protection when the token may read it) through a new GitHost method (github.ts, types.ts, memory.ts, a testenv route); when a rule requires approving reviews, a code owner's review or anything Forerunner cannot satisfy, nothing merges, neither unattended nor on the person's click, and the record says why in one sentence ('This repository needs an approving review before merging, and GitHub does not let you approve your own pull request: merge it on GitHub once someone else approved it.'); never an admin bypass; required status checks are waited for as checks. GitHub's asynchronous merge with bypass_rules false only after checking its documentation (not in /tmp/frbench/owner-q/docs; unverified); otherwise the plain endpoint pinned to the sha after the rules check. (6) onMerged(task, mergeSha, method): one callback for every merge this area makes (session, retry, resume); 'dependent-branches' fires the same callback for PRs the watcher sees merged on GitHub. (7) A new ADR (next free number at merge time) amending ADR 0062 and ADR 0106 point 6, which 'dependent-branches' and 'merge-in-app' amend; docs/maintainers/runtime.md, capabilities.md, state.md; CHANGELOG [Unreleased]. Leave room for wave 8: the record carries agent_id; sharing records between installs or people is the collaboration module's.

areas.title: A budget stop is a clean pause in the engine: Claude Code really stops and is counted once, the agent hears an 80% wrap-up on both paths when the budget leaves room for one, a run that wrapped up with work left is 'paused' (no review, no failed try), the stop names its real limit, and a run cannot eat the review share
problems: [blocker] On the subscription a budget stop does not stop Claude Code. Forerunner's check throws inside the message loop (packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:285-289); the stream is closed only when the run was aborted (:322-328), and nothing aborts it on this path; unregister() (:365) takes the run off the kill switch (enforcement/killswitch.ts:121-123), so Stop now can no longer reach it, and the hooks still allow tools after run() returned (packages/runtime/test/sdk-driver.test.ts:117-133). Claude Code can go on editing the task's folder and using the plan allowance, uncounted, until its own maxBudgetUsd (:206), maxTurns (60) or the end (read in the code and the SDK bundle; not run).

[blocker] Subscription usage is counted wrongly: every assistant message's usage is added (sdk.ts:255-283), while messages of parallel tool calls share one id and one usage and a message's output_tokens is a placeholder (Agent SDK cost-tracking docs): input counted twice, output too low, so an 80% line would fire at the wrong time.

[major] The agent is never told about its budget: the 80% 'finish current' decision is only a warning event (agent/loop.ts:371-378); the model starts new work until the call that would go over is refused (enforcement/budget.ts:103-125).

[major] A graceful wrap-up would read as done: a run that ends normally is 'completed', mapped to 'done' (session/executor.ts:1257-1269), reviewed by the critic (review money), rejected for unmet criteria and counted as a failed try on the ladder; and the Run row takes the driver's outcome (executor.ts:1281 `outcome: result.outcome`), so a graceful pause would be stored as 'completed' and 'cost''s learner would read it as a full-cost sample.

[major] On tiny budgets the per-run reserve (the larger of 20% and two worst-case calls) can be at least the run's cap, so a wrap-up line at 'cap less reserve' would fire at the first call or never (budget.ts:103-152).

[major] The run's last words are dropped at a budget stop: an error always replaces the report in the run's artifacts (executor.ts:1289-1297), so the next run reads 'It failed: The run failed: run budget would be exceeded' (task-context.ts:198-207).

[major] The real limit is not named: a stop at the month cap, the project cap or the subscription allowance (hooks.ts:156-169 throw budget_exceeded with details.level) goes down the task-budget path whenever the task's cap is below the session's (executor.ts:1331), so its card offers 'Raise the budget', which does not help; on the subscription Claude Code's own error_max_budget_usd result reads as provider_error (sdk.ts:305-311): Failed, retried as a passing glitch (read in the code, not reproduced).

[major] A running task can eat the share kept for reviews: the run's cap is the smaller of the task's cap and what the whole session has left (executor.ts:791, :824 use budget.remainingUsdMicro()), and budget.ts:139-152 lets the current call run past the work ceiling; the task's review then has no money (packages/critic/src/critic.ts, phase 'review').
decisions: budgets: Q3 yes: 80/20 wrap-up per run, paused outcome (no review, no failed try), code-side save with 'where I stopped / left to do', resume from it, card naming the real limit with 'Continue (CHF N more)' starting the next session at once, cancel sets work aside and names stuck dependents, subscription stop really stops Claude Code, better estimates and caching. (this area: 80/20 wrap-up per run, the paused outcome, the real limit's name, the subscription stop that really stops Claude Code)
root_causes: sdk.ts handles Forerunner's refusal as an exception that ends its for-await loop, not as an abort of the Claude Code process; the iterator keeps running unless the controller was aborted.
sdk.ts sums usage per assistant message instead of per message id, and never takes output tokens from the result message.
SessionBudget.precheck (budget.ts:103-152) has one 80% line for the session and none per run; the hooks return finish_current, but the loop and the SDK driver only log it.

The executor maps outcomes from the driver's outcome only (executor.ts:1257-1269), writes it to the Run row (:1281) and keeps the error over the report (:1289-1297); it reads the cap's source (runCapOf) but not the refusal's level.
executor.ts:791 uses the session's whole remainder, not its work budget (the cap less reserveShare).
areas.fix_scope: (1) The subscription first: on every budget stop (Forerunner's refusal, Claude Code's own error_max_budget_usd, the run cap) abort the run's controller and wait until Claude Code has exited (bounded; then the process is ended) before the run returns; the run stays registered with the kill switch until then; the run's token is marked ended so the hooks refuse every tool after the stop; count usage once per message id and take output tokens from the result message; maxBudgetUsd slightly above the run cap so Forerunner's own stop comes first; error_max_budget_usd reads as budget_exceeded. Prove it with a fake SDK that keeps sending messages and tool calls after the stop. (2) The 80% line per run: SessionBudget gets a per-run work line at the run's cap less a reserve, the reserve being the larger of 20% of the cap and the worst-case cost of two calls (the shared estimate function, which 'cost' later improves without a change here); the hooks return 'wrap_up' once. When that line is at or below the worst case of the run's first call (a tiny budget: the reserve is at least the cap, or leaves no room for one call), no wrap-up message is sent and the run pauses at its budget with the code-side save only (owner-answers.md section 3, option B: 'On tiny budgets 20% does not pay for one call, so only the code-side save happens'); the run's log line says which of the two applies and names the reserve. (3) The wrap-up message on both paths: the loop adds one text block after the last tool results (never inside a tool result): 'About a fifth of this task's budget is left. Start nothing new, leave the files working, and end your report with Where I stopped: and Left to do: as a list.'; the SDK path returns the same text once as additionalContext from PostToolUse. The brief says what those two headings are for. (4) 'Paused': a run is paused when it stopped at a budget (any level), or when the wrap-up message was sent in this run and its report's 'Left to do:' list has at least one item. A run that ends normally without a wrap-up in this run, or after one with no items ('Left to do: nothing'), is reviewed as usual, so a resumed run that finishes is reviewed and never loops into a new card. A paused run gets no critic and no failed try; its report is kept (the error goes beside it, not over it) and parsed into the run's artifacts as { handoff: { stopped, leftToDo, stoppedBy: 'wrap_up' | 'budget' } }, data only (JSON-quoted when read back; it may carry web text). The Run row's outcome is 'paused' for a graceful pause (written by the executor, not the driver's 'completed') and stays 'budget_exceeded' for a hard stop; 'cost''s learner skips both (a test across the two areas). The runner routes 'paused' to today's budget card until 'budget-resume' replaces it. (5) The real limit: the stop carries its level (the task's budget, the specialist's limit, the session, the project, the month, the subscription allowance) from the refusal's details into budgetStop.source, and the run's sentence names it ('stopped at this month's cap of CHF 150'); 'budget-resume''s card uses it. (6) A run's cap is at most what is left of the session's work budget (executor.ts:791, :824), so the review share stays for reviews. (7) A new ADR amending ADR 0105 (the pause, the tiny-budget rule; with today's review share about 0.8 x 0.8 = 64% of a session goes to work, as the owner was told; 'budget-resume' amends it), docs/maintainers/runtime.md, the user guide's budget text, CHANGELOG.

areas.title: Merging is safe before either mode ships (part 2): dependent branches stay true: no replay in the PR executor, a rebuild when a dependency is merged, closed or redone, a rebuild that drops a dependency never merges unseen, the watcher reports what it reads, a redo starts a fresh branch, and the PR says how to merge it
problems: [blocker] The PR executor replays a dependency's commits. dependencyBase merges with git.mergeFrom, which fast-forwards when it can (git.ts:493-497), so a branch built on a single dependency has no merge commit and hasMergesSince is false. When the task runs again after that dependency's PR was squash-merged or closed, `unmerged` is empty, so `merging` is false, execute() deletes DEPS_BASE_REF (pr-executor.ts:322-342, `git.setRef(DEPS_BASE_REF, null)`) and syncs after the run with `rebaseOnto(origin/<base>)` (:386-389), which replays the dependency's commits or keeps them silently. continueResolved (:657-691) merges whenever there are unmerged dependencies or merge commits since the base; its rebase at :691 is reached only in this same fast-forward case (the draft said it always rebased: corrected).

[blocker] The dependent-branch fix (fix/decisions cb39188, ADR 0106 point 6) leaves gaps and says something untrue. Every dependent PR says 'Merge in any order.' (pr-executor.ts:152-156), which holds only for GitHub's 'Create a merge commit' (squash-merging either PR first conflicts when the dependent edited the dependency's file: /tmp/frbench/owner-q/gitexp). A dependency whose PR is closed unmerged, or whose task is redone or cancelled, stays inside the dependent branch (unmergedDependencies :447-473 skips closed PRs, but the branch already holds the commits from :346-349) and reaches main with it, unseen. A dependency merged by squash or rebase does not rebuild the dependent branch (no code), so its PR keeps listing the dependency's files.

[major] A rebuild can drop a closed or redone dependency without a conflict. The task's own diff is then unchanged, so a reviewed version that moved with it would let the work, reviewed on top of the dependency's code, merge on a base without that code; in the automatic mode nobody would look at it in its new context.

[major] The watcher stops reading a PR once it is not open (githost-watcher.ts:466-469 marks it closed and returns no event), so a merge on GitHub by any method, a close, or an open PR's mergeable change is never reported to the rest of the app.

[major] A redo of a task whose PR was merged or closed reuses its branch name (pr-executor.ts:273-276; task.branch is kept on reopen) and looks for open PRs only (:314-317). With 'delete branch on merge' off (forerunner-sandbox), the old branch is still on GitHub, so the redo's push is not a fast-forward and is refused (read in the code, not run).

'merge-in-app' (the conflict notice) and 'merged-copy' (the copy's refresh) subscribe to these callbacks in compose.ts and do not edit the watcher. (4) PR words: until a dependent is rebuilt its PR body says 'Builds on #4 (not merged yet): this pull request includes its changes. own_folder: No (do not link the person's own working folder).
root_causes: The copy's refresh is a side effect of the session's status write (loop/docs.ts); no merge and no poll of the default branch calls it, and nothing serialises git in the copy.

(2) One lock per project copy (docs.ts): the refresh, every docs write (scaffoldProject, writeSessionStatus, the status PR) and 'merged-actions''s preview take it, so git never runs twice at once in the clone; the watcher's refresh waits for a docs write and the copy ends on the default branch. (3) 'Local only': one folder per repository project, 'Local only', in the project's copy, excluded through .git/info/exclude, listed in the Files tab with one line ('Never uploaded. Agents can read and change it.') and opened with Open folder; a repository that already tracks a path under 'Local only/' gets no such folder, with one sentence. Each task's run gets it inside its worktree, copied in before the run and back after it: never following links (a link or junction is skipped with a log line) and refusing any path that resolves outside the folder; copied back are only the files the run changed, and never a file changed in the project's copy since the copy in (the person's file wins and the agent's version is kept beside it as '<name> (from <task title>)<ext>', with one sentence in the task's result: see owner_questions); a crash between the copy in and the copy back is recovered at the next run or the daemon's start (a marker records the copy in; recovery copies back what the run changed, by the same rules). [major, supersedes fix/decisions' default] The card does not fit a pause: '"X" stopped at its budget of CHF Y' with Raise the budget / Cancel task (packages/runtime/src/session/budget-card.ts:34, :77-133); Raise sets the budget and starts a session that 'tries again' (:46-57, :350-385); a month-cap or allowance stop gets the same offer; a session-budget stop files nothing the first time and, on fix/decisions (f4cff0f, C-36, the session lead's default), a second card with Raise session budget / Raise its budget / Cancel task (budget-card.ts:36-47, :151-260; runner.ts:2022-2085).

[major] Cancel after a stop only cancels: the files stay (they are set aside only when the cancel stops a live run, ADR 0105 point 6; budget-card.ts:390-395), and the tasks that wait on it read 'Stuck: "X" was cancelled' with no card and never run (packages/runtime/src/daemon/task-words.ts:360-366).

[minor] C-30 (handoffs.json 'polish'): Undo of a cancel says 'Undone: reopened the task "X"; it is ready again and a session picks it up.' but starts no session (packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts:568 undoMoveSentence; the fake daemon's performUndo does not say it).

areas.fix_scope: (1) Save the work in code (no model): on every pause, commit 'Work in progress: <title> (paused at <limit>)' with the left-to-do list on the task's own branch in its local worktree (repository project), or as its own commit in the project's folder (folder project, so the next task's snapshot does not absorb it); push it to GitHub only when the project setting 'Push unfinished work to GitHub' is on (default off: a push starts automatic checks and co-workers see the branch; Cancel then deletes the remote branch too; the push passes 'merged-copy''s Local only check, so a file under 'Local only/' is never in it). (2) Resume: the next run of the task starts from its local branch when that holds work in progress (not checkout -B from origin), with main merged in when it moved ('merge-record''s and 'dependent-branches''s no-replay rule: a branch that holds merged-in work is brought up to date by merging, never rebased), so the git refusal is gone; a conflict goes to the existing rebase-conflict card, never a generic Failed. (3) The next brief starts with '## Where the last run stopped': the note, the files it changed and the to-do list (a run that paused without a wrap-up, on a tiny budget or at a hard stop, has no note: the section says so and lists the files it changed), quoted as data (JSON-quoted as task-context.ts does), instead of 'It failed: ...' for a pause. A resumed run that finishes and ends with 'Left to do: nothing' is reviewed ('budget-stop''s rule: a pause needs a wrap-up in this run and items left), never paused again. (4) One card per pause, at the first stop of any kind, naming the real limit from 'budget-stop''s source: '"X" paused at its budget of CHF 0.40: done ...; left ...' with 'Continue (CHF N more)' (the same amount again, at least the estimate; it raises the task's or the session's budget and starts the next session at once through resumeWork with budgetUsdMicro) and 'Cancel task'; a month cap offers no Continue but says where to change it (Settings), the subscription allowance says when it resets ('credential-limits''s waiting words). This supersedes fix/decisions' second-stop card (C-36): SESSION_BUDGET_STOP_OPTIONS and the stop count go, and a session-budget stop pauses with the same card at the first stop. (5) Cancel of a paused task sets its work in progress aside (Undo brings it back), in a folder project only while no later task has built on it (else it says the files stay, and why); the dialog and the answer name the tasks that will be stuck; C-37's sentence for a linked folder ('Its run stops now; what it wrote stays in your folder.'); C-30's undo sentence without the session promise; the fake daemon says the same. (6) Words on the task row and drawer ('Paused at its budget · Continue or cancel in the Inbox'), the session result (its own line builder appended to result.ts's list) and the notification, by design §5. (7) docs/user-guide.md (the session text that promises the next session 'continues it'; the budget text), the ADR 'budget-stop' wrote (amended), docs/maintainers/runtime.md, capabilities.md, commands.md, CHANGELOG.

areas.title: Research searches on the API key: Anthropic's web search, capped per task from the money left with its result tokens counted before the call, mixed steps, pauses and sealed results passed through unchanged, any domain-list or 'not enabled' refusal handled without failing the task, its security limits stated, and a claim sourced only once its page was opened
problems: [major] No search on the API key: cc:WebSearch has no loop equivalent (packages/runtime/src/registry/tools.ts:42-59) and the researcher's brief says so (NO_WEB_SEARCH_LINE, session/executor.ts:165-166, :888-895), so research reads only the addresses the brief names or the model guesses.

[major] The adapter would break research with server tools: it sends only Forerunner's tools (provider/anthropic.ts:252-261), drops every block but text, tool_use and tool_result when it sends the history back (toApiMessage :395-412), and maps any unknown stop reason, pause_turn included, to end_turn (mapStop :414-425). When Claude calls web_search and web_fetch in one step, the API stops with tool_use and a server_tool_use that has no result yet, which must go back unchanged with the app's tool results (/tmp/frbench/owner-q/docs/server-tools.md:399-498, 'Mixing server tools and client tools'): the common case, not an edge case. Search results carry encrypted_content that must be sent back exactly as received, or the request fails with a 400 (web-search-tool.md:590-599).

[major] Search results arrive sealed (encrypted; web-search-tool.md:597-599): the critic cannot read them, so a claim cited from a search result would be checked against nothing; today the critic's web evidence holds only pages read with web_fetch (session/web-sources.ts; loop/critic.ts:441).

[major] The budget checks cannot price a server search: one call can run several searches, at USD 10 per 1,000 searches, and their results are counted as input tokens inside the same call ('counted as input tokens, in search iterations run during a single turn', web-search-tool.md:707), before the app sees anything; the worst case and the ledger count tokens only (billing/src/pricing.ts), and adding only max_uses x USD 0.01 would let one call pass the run's cap.

[major] The domain lists can make every research call fail with a 400: the server tool refuses a wildcard in the domain ('*.example.com' is invalid) and a request-level allowed list outside the organisation's list (server-tools.md:1054-1070), and today's block list can hold '*.' patterns (wiring/browser-ports.ts:54-63 hostPatterns keeps '*.'); on the server 'example.com' covers its subdomains, unlike the capability token's domainCovered (enforcement/token.ts:231-246). Only the 'not enabled' 400 was planned for.

[major] The security limits of server search were not stated: its results reach the model without Forerunner's data envelope or injection scan (their content is encrypted to Anthropic, web-search-tool.md:597-599; agent/sdk.ts and the loop wrap only Forerunner's own tool results), the searches run inside the API, outside the hooks' per-call gate, and the optional Headroom proxy (context/headroom.ts, which speaks the Messages wire format) could alter the blocks that must go back unchanged.
[minor] An account administrator can switch web search off; the request then fails with a 400 'not enabled', which would fail the task.

[minor] Dynamic filtering is on by default for the newest search tool version and runs search from code execution (extra blocks, a container id): a first version is more reliable without it (server-tools.md:1033; web-search-tool.md:97-99).
decisions: web_search: Q5 yes: Anthropic web search on the API key (capped per task), Forerunner's page reader on both credentials, sourced only after the page was opened, information wrapper on the subscription path too. (this area: Anthropic web search on the API key, capped per task, and 'sourced only after the page was opened')
root_causes: provider/types.ts has no server-tool block, no pause_turn stop reason and no server_tool_use usage; toApiMessage rebuilds blocks from Forerunner's own types only.
The loop's turn logic ends when no client tool_use is present or the stop reason is not tool_use (agent/loop.ts:499-505).
Pricing and the ledger count tokens only (billing/src/pricing.ts costOf); the worst case knows nothing of input that arrives inside the call.
registry/tools.ts maps only WebFetch for the loop; the project's lists exist only in the capability token's pattern form.
areas.fix_scope: (1) The server tool: on the API key, a run whose specialist names cc:WebSearch and whose capability token allows web search gets Anthropic's web_search tool (a version the installed @anthropic-ai/sdk types know, without dynamic filtering: allowed_callers ['direct'] or the plain version), with max_uses from (4), and the project's lists through one resolver in wiring/web-ports.ts (today the block list as blocked_domains; 'sites' extends the resolver; never both lists in one request), each entry in the server's form: '*.example.com' sent as 'example.com' (which covers its subdomains there), an entry the server cannot take left out with one log line. (2) Pass-through: provider/types.ts gets a raw server block kept exactly as received (server_tool_use, web_search_tool_result with its encrypted content, and any block the API returns with them); toApiMessage sends it back unchanged; context compression never edits it; runs with the server tool bypass the Headroom proxy (context/headroom.ts) so nothing rewrites those blocks; 'cost''s cache breakpoint stays on a block that may carry one. (3) Mixed steps and pauses: a tool_use stop with a pending server_tool_use is answered with the client tool results while the server block stays in the assistant turn as received; pause_turn sends the paused turn back unchanged (a few continuations at most, counted against the step cap). (4) Cost before and after the call: usage.server_tool_use.web_search_requests x USD 0.01 is added to the call's cost, the ledger, the budget hooks and the Run row; the pre-call worst case adds max_uses x (USD 0.01 + a per-search allowance of result tokens at the input price), the allowance kept in pricing.ts beside the search price and set from measured searches with headroom; max_uses is the smaller of the per-task cap (10) and what the money left pays at that worst case, and 0 leaves the tool out. A call whose search usage went past its allowance is seen at the next precheck, which refuses a call that no longer fits, and the run's log names the overshoot. Each search is one audit row and one session-log line ('searched the web for ...'). (5) Refusals never fail the task: a 400 saying web search is not enabled marks search off for that key (kept; cleared when the key changes); a 400 about the domain lists (an invalid entry, an allowed list outside the organisation's) is treated the same for that project's lists; in both cases the call is made again without the tool (never without the lists), the run's log says once 'Web search is switched off for this API key; research reads pages by address.' or 'Web search refused this project's site list; research reads pages by address.', and 'credential-chooser''s capability function reads the off state. (6) Sourced only after opened: the brief says to cite only pages read with web_fetch; the critic gets the addresses seen in search but not opened beside the pages read (web-sources.ts, loop/critic.ts webSourceEvidence), and a claim that cites only those is not sourced. (7) The API key's search entry in 'credential-chooser''s capability function, and NO_WEB_SEARCH_LINE only where search is not offered. (8) The stand-in: 'credential-limits''s Messages API stand-in learns server_tool_use, web_search_tool_result (an opaque encrypted blob it checks comes back byte for byte), a mixed step, a pause_turn, a domain-list 400 and a search usage above the allowance; the bench's stand-in model plays the same, so the path runs on the bench without spending. (9) Security, stated in the ADR: server search results reach the model sealed, without Forerunner's data envelope or injection scan, and the searches run inside the API outside the hooks' per-call gate; so the run's capability token decides whether the tool is offered at all (the hooks' grant still decides), max_uses is set by code, the plain fields of each result (title, url, page_age) pass Forerunner's injection scan and a finding is flagged in the session log and to the critic, the brief says search results are information and never instructions, Stop now aborts the stream in flight (the kill switch reaches the request's signal), and pages are read only with Forerunner's web_fetch. (10) Amend ADR 0107 (points 4 and 8) or a new ADR, docs/user-guide.md (research), docs/maintainers/runtime.md, billing.md, security.md, scripts/bench/README.md, CHANGELOG.

areas.title: Actions on merged and waiting work: 'Open this version' on a waiting PR, 'Take this work out' that reverts by the way the PR was merged, and no repository created without a yes, from the chat agent too
problems: [major] A waiting PR can be looked at only on GitHub: nothing puts its files on the PC before merging (SummaryTab.tsx:308-316 offers Open on GitHub only).

[major] Nothing takes merged work out: Done is final (packages/state/src/workflow.ts:40), Undo cannot reach a merge, and no code reverts a merged PR (no revert step in capabilities, runtime or commands). A PR the person merged on GitHub by squash or rebase has a merge commit with one parent, or several rebased commits, so `git revert -m 1` on the recorded sha would fail or undo only part of it.

[major] Autopilot creates a repository without asking, on two paths: RepoProposals.consider runs repo.create itself when external_send is free at autonomy 4 (packages/runtime/src/loop/repo-create.ts:314-335; header :30-35 'at Autopilot the agent runs repo.create itself'), and the repo.create command rates a private repository 'low' risk for an agent at autonomy 4 (packages/commands/src/commands/repo.ts:63-71; header :14-20), so the conversation agent, whose command tools run with actor kind agent (packages/runtime/src/loop/commands.ts:275), creates one with no card.

[minor] C-60 (handoffs.json 'polish'): a finished folder project reads 'Waiting for you: 1 question' on Home because of the 'Create a repository?' offer (holdsTask counts every open card but Docker's: packages/runtime/src/daemon/task-words.ts:178-183; project-status.ts:153-162); the card says '... with no branch, pull request or review on GitHub' (repo-create.ts:341), and design §3.8 does not list this card. Expected: a non-blocking offer never makes a project read 'Waiting for you'; its words follow design §5.
decisions: pr_preview: 'Open this version' on a waiting PR: its files on the PC to try before merging.

merging: GitHub projects: default 'you press Merge' with a one-click Merge in the app (dependency order, merge commits only, the safe merge step); per-project option 'merge automatically after review'; 'Take this work out' (revert PR naming later tasks that built on it). Each task's agent keeps committing on its own branch. (this area: 'Take this work out')
autopilot_repo: Autopilot asks before creating a repository (no silent creation).
root_causes: No preview checkout exists; the pull-request view has no action besides its link.
githost has no revert step, and nothing reads how a PR was merged (merge commit, squash or rebase).
repo-create.ts and repo.ts decide by the autonomy table (decideAutonomy('external_send')) instead of always asking.
areas.fix_scope: (1) 'Open this version' on each waiting PR (task and docs): POST /projects/:id/pull-requests/:number/preview (real daemon and fake daemon in the same commit) checks the PR's head out into a preview folder beside the copy (git worktree add --detach, under 'merged-copy''s per-copy lock), answers with the folder, and the Overview shows it with Open folder and one sentence ('#7 as it would be merged. Changes here are not kept.'); the preview is replaced by the next one and removed when the PR is merged or closed (onMerged, onPullRequestState); nothing runs there and Local only is not copied into it. (2) 'Take this work out' on a merged task (drawer and Tasks row): POST /tasks/:id/take-out makes a branch from main and reverts by the way the PR was merged: from the record's method and merge sha (Forerunner's merges are merge commits: git revert -m 1), or, for a PR merged on GitHub, from the merge commit's parents and the PR's commits: two parents, git revert -m 1; one parent and the PR's commits not on main (a squash), git revert <sha> without -m; a rebase merge, a revert of the PR's commits on main ending at the merge sha, each matched to the PR's commits by patch id; anything else is refused with one sentence ('#4 was merged in a way Forerunner cannot undo safely; undo it on GitHub.'). It pushes the branch and opens a pull request 'Take out: <title>' whose body and the answer name the later tasks that built on it (done tasks that depend on it); it never pushes to main; a revert that conflicts files one card in words; the task row says 'Taken out in #9 (waiting for you to merge)', and the PR is listed under Waiting for you to merge with 'merge-in-app''s Merge (it has no record, so it merges on the click). (3) Autopilot asks: RepoProposals always files the card (remove the autopilot branch, repo-create.ts:314-335, and say so in its header); repo.create rates a private repository 'medium' for every actor at every level (drop the agent-at-Autopilot 'low' exception, repo.ts:63-71, and its header), so the chat agent's repo.create files a card too; the card's words follow design §5 (no '... with no branch, pull request or review on GitHub'). (4) C-60: the offer is not counted as a question in Home's line (holdsTask or the card's kind; 'polish' owns project-status.ts's words). areas.title: Research may read any public website, with per-project 'only these' or 'never these' lists that work the same on both credentials and in one stored list, never this PC or the home network, Forerunner's page reader on the subscription too, a loopback seam no person can reach, and a settings row and a project-page line
problems: [major] The site list means the opposite of its name: settings.browser.allowedDomains lets a listed host be read on a private or local address (packages/capabilities/src/web/policy.ts:13-15, addressAllowed :182-184), and there is no 'only these sites' mode. The same list is also the browser binding's and the sandbox's network list (daemon/compose.ts:1096, :1907, :2791; daemon/sandbox-port.ts:74), so it cannot simply be reread as 'only these'.

[major] Putting 'localhost' or '127.0.0.1' on the site list opens this PC to research, the app's own daemon included (policy.ts:182-184; the daemon listens on 127.0.0.1 and its token guards every route but /health, daemon/server.ts).

[major] Blocking 'facebook.com' does not block 'www.facebook.com': matching is exact unless an entry starts with '*.' (enforcement/token.ts:231-246 domainCovered, used by web/policy.ts:128, :171, by browser/policy.ts:65 and by the capability token's own checks, token.ts:136), so widening domainCovered itself would widen every tool's domain check.
[major] An entry pasted as 'https://example.com/page' is dropped without a word (wiring/browser-ports.ts:54-63 hostPatterns).

[major] Blocks can be written through two places: settings.browser.blockedDomains through PUT /projects/:id/settings, and the new setting; a one-time move into the new list would leave blocks written later through the old route enforced but not shown.

[minor] C-70 (handoffs.json 'polish'): 'http://example.com./' is read although example.com is blocked: hostOfUrl lowercases and strips IPv6 brackets only, no trailing dot (policy.ts:113-115). Expected: hostOfUrl strips one trailing '.'; unit tests for the block list and the site list with it.
[major] No screen sets either list (C-66): PUT /projects/:id/settings needs a version the project view does not carry; fix/decisions' user guide says there is no screen.

[major] On the subscription no page is opened: Claude Code's WebFetch is checked against the run's allowed domains (agent/cc-tools.ts:77-82; enforcement/hooks.ts:321-333), empty for the researcher, so every page is refused; Forerunner's own reader is not offered there (sdk.ts:196-214 sets no tool server).

[major] On the subscription web text reaches the model without the 'information, not instructions' wrapper: the hook returns updatedMCPToolOutput (agent/sdk.ts:485-487), which Claude Code applies to MCP tools only (SDK types sdk.d.ts:2724-2731: updatedToolOutput).

root_causes: policy.ts treats the site list as 'named hosts may be private' and matches with the capability token's exact-or-wildcard domainCovered.
browser-ports.ts keeps only bare host patterns and drops the rest silently; the lists live under settings.browser, shared with the browser binding and the sandbox.
The SDK path has no tool server for Forerunner's tools and keeps Claude Code's WebFetch, checked against the token's empty domain list.

areas.fix_scope: (1) Reader rules (policy.ts, fetch.ts), with the reader's own matcher: mode 'any' (the default) with a 'never' list, or 'only' with a list that may not be empty; each entry covers the site and its subdomains in the page reader's matcher only (enforcement/token.ts domainCovered, used by the hooks, the browser policy and the token, is not changed); trailing dots and case normalised (C-70); always refused whatever any list says: loopback (localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1, 0.0.0.0/8), link-local and metadata addresses, names without a dot, private and home-network addresses (a list no longer opens them), the 6to4 range checked. (2) A loopback seam no person can reach: a composition option that only the development provider modes set, those that load testenv/ from a repository checkout and play a scripted model (--provider bench and 'credential-limits''s --provider bench-api); never --provider bench-live against the real API, never an environment variable (FORERUNNER_BENCH_LIVE_API included), a config.json field or a setting. research-web.test.ts, web-fetch.test.ts, real-daemon.test.ts, scripts/bench/README.md and 'web-search''s bench walk move onto it; a bench-live dry run against a local stand-in is replaced by bench-api. (3) The setting 'Web pages research may read' (settings.set key web_access {mode, only, never}) with one shared clean-up (lowercase; strip scheme, path, port, a trailing dot and a leading www.; ASCII or punycode; refuse IP addresses, local names, and public suffixes such as co.uk or github.io in the 'only' list), shown back before saving and never dropped silently; widening asks a yes (compared with the current value at save: new code in settings.set), narrowing applies at once. One stored block list: web_access.never; a write of settings.browser.blockedDomains through PUT /projects/:id/settings is taken into web_access.never in the same write, with an audit row (real-daemon case and fake daemon in the same commit); until a project's settings are written, the reader and the row read both keys, so every block in force is enforced and shown; browserSettingsOf's blockedDomains returns the same list, so the browser binding enforces it too. settings.browser.allowedDomains is ignored by the reader and never turned into 'only' (it stays the browser binding's and the sandbox's), and the setting's row says so in one sentence. (4) A row in Settings (Per project) and one line on the project page ('Research reads: any public website · Change'), in its own small component of SummaryTab.tsx (not RepositoryFiles, not ProjectPage.tsx). (5) The brief names the project's rule and asks the report to say what it could not read because of it; the intake sees an 'only' list and plans no research that needs other sites. (6) Both credentials: on the subscription Forerunner's page reader is offered through the SDK's in-process tool server with alwaysLoad true (the provider/claude-code.ts:278-290 pattern; without it the hooks refuse the tool-search step); Claude Code's WebFetch is switched off (disallowedTools and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WEB_FETCH); Claude Code's WebSearch gets the lists through updatedInput in PreToolUse (merging with the model's own lists: 'never' entries removed from its allowed list; in 'only' mode only the overlap kept, and the search refused in words when nothing is left); PostToolUse uses updatedToolOutput with the data wrapper for the reader and for WebSearch; the executor logs the pages on the subscription branch too (withWebSourceLog); the run says plainly when the init message's tool list lacks the reader or search. The server search on the API key ('web-search') gets the same lists through web-ports.ts (allowed_domains in 'only' mode, blocked_domains otherwise, never both, in the server's form; left out of the run with a log line when a 'never' entry sits inside an 'only' entry). (7) The capability function's subscription entry can now read pages, so research follows the person's order where both credentials can search and read; SEARCH_ONLY_LINE, webSearchOnly and SEARCH_ONLY_LIMITATION go (executor.ts:152-162, :896-903; compose.ts:693-698, :3856; model-settings-view.ts:61-64, :192; api-types.ts:1614), with their words in BillingOrderSection.tsx and NewTaskDialog.tsx. (8) Proxy: when the PC has a proxy set (HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY; the Windows system setting if it can be read) and a direct connection fails, the refusal says 'This computer reaches the internet through a proxy, which Forerunner's page reader does not use yet: pages cannot be read here; web search still works.', and the Settings row says it too. (9) C-71's user guide line; an ADR (0107 addendum or new, amending 'web-search''s if it wrote one), docs/maintainers/capabilities.md, browser.md, runtime.md, security.md, CHANGELOG.

areas.title: Leftovers of wave 7, merge side: same-titled tasks never share a branch, and the merge, rebuild, take-out and copy paths keep true state across busy worktrees, crashes and redos
problems: [major] Two tasks with the same title created in one repository within about 65 s get the same branch fr/<first 8 hex of the UUIDv7>-<slug>; the second finds the first's open pull request by branch name, resumes it and pushes its own work onto it. Evidence: Verified at fa1a86f. packages/capabilities/src/githost/pr-executor.ts:667-670 branch = fr/${task.id.slice(0, 8)}-<slug> (no deps.branchFor is wired anywhere); packages/platform/src/ids.ts:4-14 newId puts the top 32 bits of the 48-bit ms timestamp in those 8 hex characters, so they change only every 65,536 ms. pr-executor.ts:708-711 looks the open PR up by head branch alone, :720 sets resume, :743-745 checks out origin/<branch>, :908 pushes with force and :2176-2186 updates the first task's PR. Polish problems[33] (C-59, no id on screen) must keep the name unique.

[minor] A crash or app close in the middle of a run leaves uncommitted files in the task's worktree with no work-in-progress commit; the next run carries them over, or git refuses its checkout ('untracked working tree files would be overwritten'). Evidence: Verified: pr-executor.ts:661-821 executeIn never checks git.status().dirty before the resume checkout (:743-745) or createBranch (:821, 'checkout -B', git.ts:439); the work-in-progress save (:830-835) and the leftovers set aside run only after inner.execute returns. W6-24 again, for crashes.

[minor] The merge retry pass and the start-up resume: a merge they make posts no Inbox Update or notification (design §3.8), and every retry of a waiting record is a full gated merge_pr call (its own token, one audit row, about 5 GitHub calls) per record per minute for up to 1440 tries. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:2508-2511 onMerged only logs and emits a project refresh; packages/runtime/src/loop/merge.ts:884-905 retryWaiting -> mergeRecorded -> run (:1120-1180: ownToken tokens.issue at :1160, mayMerge :685-741 reads no checks), beforeToolCall :1303-1305 writes the audit row; MAX_MERGE_ATTEMPTS :84 = 1440; resumeAtStart :913-950 files nothing. ADR 0111:246-249 known gap.

[minor] The card filed when a rebuild voids a review is merge-record's left-open card: 'I merged it' (primary) and 'Leave it open'. 'I merged it' notes 'merged by you' on the task while the PR is still open; the body says 'or send it back' with no button; neither Merge nor Redo is offered. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/session/dependent-branches.ts:294-305 calls fileLeftOpenRequest with no options, so loop/merge.ts:1679/:1710 MERGE_LEFT_OPEN_OPTIONS apply; session/pr-answers.ts:98 and :197-202 patch the task reason 'merged by you: <url>' without asking the host; request-words.ts:845-853 makes the first option primary; body text dependent-branches.ts:84.

[MOVED to leftovers7-merge2 in wave 14: not this area's, not a review finding here] [minor] Rebuilds that could not run (busy or dirty worktree, failed step) are remembered only in memory: a squash-merge or close seen while the dependent's worktree was busy, followed by a restart, is never rebuilt, so the dependent's PR keeps the dependency's commits and files. Evidence: Verified: dependent-branches.ts:108-109 owed is an in-memory Map, filled by rebuildFor (:194-206); sweep (:177-190) refinds only dependencies that are not done. ADR 0111:182-184 known gap.

[MOVED to leftovers7-merge2 in wave 14: not this area's, not a review finding here] [minor] No shared worktree lock: a merge already under way when a dependency closes can still finish before the rebuild pushes, and ReviewedPrMerge's own git steps in a task worktree (the update path of mergeChecked) are not serialised with a rebuild of that worktree. Evidence: Verified: pr-executor.ts:300-321 worktreesInUse/inWorktree/tryWorktree are private to the module; loop/merge.ts:361, :530 and :826 build GitOps on the task worktree without them; the rebuild voids the record first (dependent-branches.ts:213 settleRecord) but does not stop a host merge call already started. ADR 0111:183-184.

[MOVED to leftovers7-merge2 in wave 14: not this area's, not a review finding here] [minor] Chain of three: if the middle task's worktree is busy when the first is squash-merged, the third follows the rebuilt middle through rebuiltTo and is not rebuilt, so its PR keeps the first task's pre-squash commits and files (the U-028 symptom) until the middle merges. Evidence: Verified: pr-executor.ts:1428-1429 tryWorktree skips the busy middle; heldState (:1220-1257) maps the third's old middle sha through rebuiltTo (:1268) and counts it as open, so the third is not rebuilt.

[minor] A redo's new PR moves a merged merge record back to queued outside the state graph and clears its take-out fields: Redo is offered while a take-out PR is open, and that PR is then no longer listed or settled. [minor] Take this work out on a dependent PR that GitHub merged with a merge commit carrying its dependency's commits reverts the merge whole with -m 1, so the dependency's work goes too. Evidence: Verified: pr-executor.ts:2245-2254 takeOutPlan returns {how:'merge', commits:[mergeSha], mainline:true} for any two-parent commit, without checking whether the merged side holds another task's record's commits. ADR 0113:201-204. Only after a merge made on GitHub out of dependency order.

problems: [major] A critic review refused at the project's budget counts as a failed try: the review becomes an 'escalate' verdict, the retry ladder runs up to 4 times and files '"X" failed 4 times' instead of pausing the task at the project's budget. Evidence: Verified at fa1a86f. packages/critic/src/critic.ts:519-526 gives outcome budget_exceeded (runOutcomeOf :1139-1148) when no verdict was captured; buildVerdict :713-724 then sets verdict 'escalate' with the high finding 'Critic review did not complete (budget_exceeded)'. packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:2955-3018 (reviewTask) emits it as an ordinary critic.verdict and :1880-1990 hands it to the ladder; nothing maps an outer-limit refusal of the review to the paused outcome that the owner's budgets decision ('paused outcome (no review, no failed try)') and ADR 0112 point 6 require. packages/runtime/test/budget-pause.test.ts:148-160 already takes projectBudgetUsdMicro.

[minor] A critic review that meets a refused or resting credential (no other credential may serve it) does not wait: it becomes an escalate verdict (or a review-failed card when the critic throws), the person gets a second card beside the refused card, and the review never runs by itself at the reset or after a new key. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/agent/loop.ts:692-704 throws USAGE_LIMIT_CODE/provider_auth, outcomeFor :1199-1210 makes it 'error', critic.ts:713-724 turns any run without a verdict into 'escalate'; runner.ts:1902-1966 files fileReviewFailedRequest for a thrown review. Neither consults credentialWaitOf. Same place as R-criticbudget. ADR 0100 points 9 and 12 ('the work that needs it waits').

[minor] Under 'Wait' the session ends at the first task that must wait and skips the rest of the queue, including tasks whose first usable credential can serve now; the project-level wait label is put on every ready task. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:1768-1777 pushes the whole queue onto skipped and stops with CREDENTIAL_WAIT_STOP at the first credentialWait; packages/runtime/src/daemon/task-words.ts:610-615 gives every ready task ctx.credentialWait (credentialWaitRow, task-display.ts:101-127). areas.title: Leftovers of wave 7, web and credentials side: the agent browser keeps its sandbox, the site rule never fails open, the subscription's hooks and bookings are right, and credential waits and the chooser say and do what is true
problems: [major] The open-web agent browser drops Chromium's own sandbox after any first launch failure (a profile lock, a timeout), not only a sandbox one, and keeps running without it for the rest of the process; the log says it runs without the sandbox whatever the cause. Evidence: Verified: packages/capabilities/src/browser/profile.ts:328-340: the catch around the chromiumSandbox:true launch sets unsandboxed for every error (launchRefusal :184-191 only picks a line) and every later launch uses chromiumSandbox:false (W6-30). A silent loss of a security boundary on the browser that reads any public site.

[minor] The site rule fails open: a stored 'Only these websites' whose entries the clean-up no longer accepts reads as 'any public website'. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/wiring/web-access.ts:437-438 only = cleanSiteList(...).sites; mode = 'only' only while an entry survives, else 'any'. Never entries are kept as written (blockEntry :452-455). Not reachable through settings.set today; a PUBLIC_SUFFIXES or LOCAL_SUFFIX change or a value written by another install (shared store) would widen research silently.

[minor] On the subscription, a built-in file read (Read, NotebookRead, Grep) gets updatedToolOutput as a bare string: Claude Code ignores or rejects the shape, so repository text reaches Claude without the 'information, not instructions' envelope, and a hook error may be logged on every file read. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:788-797 marks Read/NotebookRead/Grep untrusted (repo_file; isRepoReadCcTool :1018-1019); :838-842 sends updatedToolOutput: builtInOutput(...), which returns the bare wrapped string for any tool but WebSearch and WebFetch (:897-907). The comment at :824-825 says a file read is 'not changed'. ADR 0107:307-309. No test asserts Read's PostToolUse return.

[minor] On the subscription, what Claude Code still reports after a stop is not booked: a killed run's late messages are never read, and after Stop all revokes the run's token a late booking fails and is only logged, so the ledger and the plan share miss the run's tail. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:578-583 returns the iterator without draining on 'killed'; :636-650 catches a failed late booking and logs 'a stopped run's late message was not booked'; packages/runtime/src/enforcement/hooks.ts:248-250 afterModelCall verifies the (revoked) token before it records.

[minor] On the subscription, Claude Code's modelUsage totals, summed over every model (subagents, Haiku auxiliary calls), are booked at the run model's price. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:1063-1081 resultTotals adds every model's tokens into one Usage; :396-402 books usageLeft(total, usage) through book(), which prices with req.pricing.cost (:296-300), the run model's price.

[minor] After a change from the Overview, the 'Research reads:' line keeps the value it set, so a later change made in chat (Talk on the Overview) leaves the line stale while the page is open. Evidence: Verified: apps/ui/src/pages/project/SummaryTab.tsx:247-252 line = changed ?? project?.researchReads; changed is set at :284 and never cleared.

[minor] A wait on a refused API key stays until that key is replaced: if the person adds a subscription instead, the ready tasks still read 'Waits for a new API key' and nothing starts by itself, although Start would run them on the subscription. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/daemon/task-display.ts:101-127 credentialWaitRow labels the project from any source that keeps it in limits.waiting and is refused, without asking whether a pick serves now; wiring/billing-pick.ts:784-813 takeReady keeps the list while the refusal stands; credentialSaved('subscription') (:826) ends only the subscription's refusal; with no order set task runs put the subscription first (docs/decisions/0100:58-60).

[minor] A billing source's limits are read and written back whole without a version check (rest, refuse, noteWait, takeReady, credentialSaved): a write landing at the same moment is lost (a waiting entry, so the rows go back to Ready with no automatic start, or restingUntil, costing one more refused call). Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/wiring/billing-pick.ts:765-775 (noteWait) and :784-813 (takeReady) read the row and patch a limits object built from the stale copy; the store has update(id, expectedVersion, patch) (packages/state/src/repos/base.ts:270-286).

[minor] The credential wake takes the waiting entries off the source before asking the scheduler for a start: a start that fails later, or is queued and lost when the app quits, loses its wait and the rows go back to plain Ready. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:3391-3416 taskBilling.takeReady() removes the entries, then scheduler.request(); the scheduler's queue is in memory and a background start that fails is only logged (packages/runtime/src/session/triggers.ts:428-450).

[minor] A session start requested while a planning call runs (Start on another project, the credential wake, a schedule) is refused with 'already working in another session', and a start the scheduler asked for is lost. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/session/intake.ts:1546-1555 inserts a session for the agent that the scheduler does not know of; triggers.ts:428-436 checks only its own active set and starts at once; runner.ts:757-763 throws claim_conflict, only logged for a background start (triggers.ts:441-450); compose.ts:3420-3426 avoids it only within one wake.

Evidence: Verified (moved from polish_add: the start check lacks the data, not only the words): packages/runtime/src/daemon/start-blocked.ts:50-96 names the intake's plan wait (:73-80) and the stopped and no-model cases but has no input for a task-level credential wait; credentialWaitRow (task-display.ts:101-127) already has the words and the save link; StartSessionDialog.tsx:242-246 shows only what the check gives.

Evidence: Verified (moved from polish_add: the chooser gets no mark): packages/runtime/src/wiring/billing-pick.ts:652-669 savedKinds keeps refused and resting kinds by design; compose.ts:4384-4395 feeds it to credentialChoiceFor.

[minor] New task's runs-on line is computed from the specialist only, never from the typed words: a task whose outcome needs the owner's decision runs on the API key (money) while New task said otherwise. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:2453-2462 calls rt.chooser.forTask({specialist, projectId}) with no task; needsOf reads the words only when given (compose.ts:4386-4390); apps/ui/src/pages/project/NewTaskDialog.tsx:133 shows the line.

areas.title: Leftovers of wave 7, merge side, part 2: rebuilds survive a restart and never race a merge, a chain of three is rebuilt whole, a pull request that stops being mergeable is said, and Files says when this computer's copy stops following
problems: [minor] Rebuilds that could not run (busy or dirty worktree, failed step) are remembered only in memory: a squash-merge or close seen while the dependent's worktree was busy, followed by a restart, is never rebuilt, so the dependent's PR keeps the dependency's commits and files. Evidence: Verified: dependent-branches.ts:108-109 owed is an in-memory Map, filled by rebuildFor (:194-206); sweep (:177-190) refinds only dependencies that are not done. ADR 0111:182-184 known gap.

[minor] No shared worktree lock: a merge already under way when a dependency closes can still finish before the rebuild pushes, and ReviewedPrMerge's own git steps in a task worktree (the update path of mergeChecked) are not serialised with a rebuild of that worktree. Evidence: Verified: pr-executor.ts:300-321 worktreesInUse/inWorktree/tryWorktree are private to the module; loop/merge.ts:361, :530 and :826 build GitOps on the task worktree without them; the rebuild voids the record first (dependent-branches.ts:213 settleRecord) but does not stop a host merge call already started. ADR 0111:183-184.

[minor] Chain of three: if the middle task's worktree is busy when the first is squash-merged, the third follows the rebuilt middle through rebuiltTo and is not rebuilt, so its PR keeps the first task's pre-squash commits and files (the U-028 symptom) until the middle merges. Evidence: Verified: pr-executor.ts:1428-1429 tryWorktree skips the busy middle; heldState (:1220-1257) maps the third's old middle sha through rebuiltTo (:1268) and counts it as open, so the third is not rebuilt.

[minor] No conflict notice: an open task PR whose mergeable turned false after another merge is never noticed; the Overview row keeps offering Merge and no card is filed (merge-in-app fix_scope 6 acceptance unmet). Evidence: Verified: compose.ts:4108-4112 passes open PRs to dependentBranches.pullRequestState, which returns at once for state open (dependent-branches.ts:120); mergeable=false is read only when Merge is pressed (loop/merge.ts:437-449). ADR 0111:246-249.

[minor] When this computer's copy cannot be brought to what is merged (a tracked file the person edited is changed by a merge, an ignored file in the way, a 'local only/' path in another case on Windows), Files keeps 'As merged on GitHub, updated HH:MM' and never says why it stopped following. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:716-724 and compose.ts:2461-2470 only log 'this computer's copy of the repository not refreshed'; CopyView (docs.ts:200-205) has no field for a copy that stopped following. ADR 0113 'Known limits'.

[minor] A merge made later by the retry pass or the start-up resume now files an Inbox Update 'Merged #N' (leftovers7-merge, R-mergeretry, merged at a2caf52) but raises no desktop notification, unlike a merge the person makes or a session makes (design §3.8). Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6a-fix-merge.json not_done: the Update is filed from loop/merge.ts; the notifier is wired in compose.ts (one small hunk is allowed here).
root_causes: packages/runtime/src/session/dependent-branches.ts: owed is an in-memory Map (filled by rebuildFor; sweep re-finds only dependencies that are not done); pullRequestState returns at once for an open PR, so mergeable=false is never read until Merge is pressed (loop/merge.ts).

packages/capabilities/src/githost/pr-executor.ts: worktreesInUse/inWorktree/tryWorktree are module-private; packages/runtime/src/loop/merge.ts builds GitOps on the task worktree without them; the rebuild voids the record but does not stop a host merge call already under way.
