areas.fix_scope: One commit per problem, the failing test first. Order: R-lock first (a merge of an unrebuilt head is the worst outcome), then R-chain, R-owed, R-conflict, R-copystuck, the notification. Line numbers in the evidence are from fa1a86f: leftovers7-merge (merged at a2caf52, its report in /tmp/frbench/wave7g6a-fix-merge.json) changed pr-executor.ts, dependent-branches.ts, merge.ts and docs.ts since, so re-find each place at HEAD and reuse what it added (taskBranchName, cleanAfterCutShortRun, the retry pass's check-first path and its Update, the rebuild card's Merge/Redo in request-words.ts) rather than duplicating it. R-lock: one exported worktree lock (from pr-executor or a small module beside it) used by PrExecutor's rebuilds and by ReviewedPrMerge's git steps in a task worktree; a rebuild that voids a record must also make a merge call already under way for that record end without merging the unrebuilt head (check the head sha the host would merge, or hold the lock across the call). R-owed: persist owed rebuilds (a new migration 0008, or a column on merge_record) with the SQLite and Postgres suite (packages/state/test/suite.ts) and a restart test; data-model.md says what the new state means. R-conflict: the watcher reads mergeable for open task pull requests (bounded: only when the base moved, not every poll for every PR), files one card per pull request (deduped across polls and restarts), and the Overview row stops offering a Merge that cannot work; the compose.ts wiring is one small hunk. R-copystuck: a new CopyView field with the reason, GET /projects/:id/files carries it (fake daemon in the same commit, a real-daemon.test.ts case), and the Files line says the copy stopped following and why. Words: polish (wave 13, after this wave) owns the wording; where a new sentence is unavoidable follow design §5 (one sentence read at a glance, CHF only, no ids) and list it in notes_for_other_areas. apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts and apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts are append-only (own describe block). Do not change runner.ts, executor.ts, recovery.ts, critic.ts, session-review.ts, intake.ts, start-check.ts, plan-tasks.ts or conversation/agent.ts (leftovers7-session's, merged), nor web-access.ts, agent/sdk.ts, enforcement/hooks.ts, billing-pick.ts, credential-choice.ts, start-blocked.ts, triggers.ts, browser/profile.ts (leftovers7-web's, running beside you). compose.ts: leftovers7-web owns the credential wake and the chooser; you may add one small hunk for the conflict watcher's wiring and one for the notifier of a later merge, and say so. Docs: runtime.md (rebuilds, the merge lock, the conflict notice, the copy), data-model.md, ADR 0111 (its known gaps at 'Known gaps' close) and ADR 0113 ('Known limits': the copy that stops following) amendments.

problems: [major] TM-1: a redo from main (the conflict notice's or the rebuild card's Redo) or 'Drop the branch and retry from scratch' whose run changes nothing, on a task with an open pull request, force-pushes main's head to the task branch: the task is done with an empty pull request that the app offers for Merge (bench run 2 of the merge2 fix-up: PR #4 merged with no diff). Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fixup-leftovers7-merge2.json new_problems[0]; pr-executor.ts execute: `!commit.committed && !existingPr` (:878 at ce13bb1) is the only no-change check, and with `dropped` the branch starts at the base.

[minor] TM-2: cleanAfterCutShortRun runs before conflictAnswer: a person who resolves a rebase conflict in the task folder (the card's 'branch only on this computer' steps) and answers 'I resolved it' with the rebase still in progress has the half-done resolution aborted. Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-merge.json non_blocking[1], /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fixup-leftovers7-merge.json not_done[1] (suggested fix: skip abortUnfinished while the task's last conflict answer is 'resolved' and not consumed).

[minor] TM-3: an unconsumed 'dropped' answer (the conflict card's Drop, a Redo from main) drops a paused run's work in progress at the next run: if the redo's run pauses (budget, a question) before review, the next run starts from main again (executeIn: wip = dropped ? null : …). Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fixup-leftovers7-merge.json not_done[5] and new_problems[1]; the fix-up's reason not to consume the mark at branch creation (the next run would merge the old conflicting branch into the work in progress) is the constraint to respect.

[minor] TM-4: Merge pressed while a rebuild is owed because the task's folder holds changes nobody committed: the record waits 'queued' and the row reads 'Merging…' with no reason until the folder is cleaned; meanwhile 'dependent branch not rebuilt: its worktree has uncommitted changes' is logged as a WARN at every poll. Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fix-leftovers7-merge2.json not_done[0]; /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-merge2.json non_blocking[2] (bench walk 3 step 14) and [7].

[minor] TM-5: possible watcher stall (not reproduced): lookFor().baseChange, keepsOwnChange and mergeChecked's update path wait on inWorktree, and PrTaskExecutor.execute holds the folder for a whole run; a done task redone while its record is queued or waiting_checks would make retryWaitingMerges, which the watcher's poll awaits, block every poll until the redo ends (no PR events, copy refreshes or conflict notices meanwhile). Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-merge2.json non_blocking[3]; /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fixup-leftovers7-merge2.json not_done[1].

[minor] TM-6: copyStoppedOf (loop/docs.ts) matches git's English messages, and GitOps (capabilities githost/git.ts) runs git with the process's locale: on a git that prints in another language the Files line falls back to 'Git could not bring it to what is merged…' without the file names. Check the other places that parse git's messages (rebase and merge conflict files) for the same dependence. Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-merge2.json non_blocking[4]; /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fixup-leftovers7-merge2.json not_done[0].

[minor] TM-7: a record whose left-to-you sentence said something else (rebuilt_without's 'reviewed with #A's changes…' warning, 'builds on #X, which was not merged: merge #X first') loses it after a conflict is resolved: conflict_resolved sets the sentence to ''. The row then offers a plain Merge without the earlier warning. Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-merge2.json non_blocking[5]; /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fixup-leftovers7-merge2.json not_done[2].

[minor] TM-8: the project page's Create a repository dialog files its pending card on Preview; closing the dialog with × or Escape leaves that card open in the Inbox (CreateRepoDialog.tsx finish() does not answer result.pendingId). Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-fixup-leftovers7-merge.json new_problems[0] (walk-repo-B.json 'afterPreview', steps/05-b-preview-shown.png).

[minor] TM-9: CopyRecord.stopped (the copy's 'stopped following' state, a file in the copy's .git) is persisted state with no restart test (validation rule 4); the bench showed it survives restart-daemon.mjs. Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-merge2.json non_blocking[1].

Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-web.json non_blocking[2].

[minor] TR-3: compose.ts credentialWaitNow builds the pick without the task's answered state and with modelTier fixed to 'sonnet': a task whose person questions were answered still gets the askPerson need, so the Start check can say 'Nothing can run yet' while the real run would go to the subscription. Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-web.json non_blocking[4].

[minor] TR-5: intake.ts onlyWebsitesLines with an empty 'only' list gives the planner '…only these websites and their subdomains: . Plan no research…' (model-facing; a sibling of R-failopen). Evidence: /tmp/frbench/wave7g6c-review-leftovers7-web.json non_blocking[5]; intake.ts:473.

[minor] TR-6: person-questions.ts isPersonTask still matches PERSONS_ANSWER on legacy titles without the RECORDED_ANSWER exception (a sibling of R-personsanswers); and RECORDED_ANSWER removes the need for a whole text, so 'Follow the owner's decision in docs/x and get the owner's confirmation before deploying' loses the confirmation need unless NEEDS_PERSON catches it. decisions: W15-01 (only the safety part, until the owner answers W15-112): an ownership marker in the status and scaffold PR bodies; a project never pushes to, comments on or lists another project's status or scaffold PR; while another project's status PR is open on fr/status this project writes none and its status stays in the app (one log line says why); with none open, today's behaviour; a legacy PR without a marker belongs to a project only when it is the only one on this install linked to the repository. No per-project branch and no second PR.

W15-02: a local commit ahead of origin on a done task's branch that is not Forerunner's own (its work-in-progress commit, its base merge, a rebuild whose push failed) holds the rebuild with one sentence and is never reset; Forerunner's own unpushed states rebuild as today.

W15-03: a dependency whose rebuild was busy, held, failed or conflicted holds the tasks that build on it as owed in the same pass; a clean same-own-change rebuild clears a stale rebuild_conflict (sentence, last_outcome and card).

W15-04: the Tasks tab's Redo on a done task with an open merge card answers that card as the card's own Redo does (redo from main, the card closed 'redone') in the same transaction, and starts no session: the owner question on Tasks-row actions stays open.

W15-05: the person's approval stays recorded and the merge goes on once the folder is clean; the held-by-changes fact is persisted on the record at the poll and shown on the row before and after the press.

W15-06: both 'I resolved it' and 'Drop the branch and retry from scratch' start or queue a session through resumeWork, as every Inbox answer that makes a task runnable does (design §3.8); Cancel starts nothing.
W15-07: a null mergeable is re-read within the same poll (a few seconds apart, capped at about 15 s in all), never by a busy loop.
W15-08: ids that code reads move to a hidden HTML-comment marker (one form shared with W15-01's ownership marker); the reader accepts the old visible form for PRs opened by earlier versions.

W15-55: one label per merge record outcome in task-words.ts's merge-state branch (now w15-merge's), agreeing with the Overview row (design §2: one status map), including the states W15-03 and W15-05 add.

W15-64: emptiedSentence's two failing forms, 'main already has this change.' and the up_to_date PR comment are reworded to the texts in the acceptance; owedFolderSentence was checked against design §5 and stays (W15-05's tests can assert it).
W15-68: the waiting_checks sentence and label are chosen by the outcome's status ('#4 merges once GitHub answers.' for an unreachable host).
root_causes: packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts: the status branch and PR belong to the repository, not to a project (fixed name, PR reused by head only, ownership approved for any fr/status PR, no marker).

packages/capabilities/src/githost/pr-executor.ts rebuildDependents/rebuildIn: a busy middle does not hold its dependents; a local commit is reset to origin; only uncommitted changes count as the person's.

packages/runtime/src/session/dependent-branches.ts and loop/merge.ts: conflict state is cleared only from last_outcome 'conflict'; a new review or a clean rebuild leaves stale cards; the watcher reads mergeable once per 60 s poll and drops null.

packages/runtime/src/daemon/pull-requests.ts / loop/merge-mode.ts: the merge route answers from canMerge before the folder state is known, and the record never carries that state until the merge step runs.
packages/runtime/src/session/pr-answers.ts: only the rebuild card's Redo resumes work; the rebase-conflict card has no words of its own.
packages/capabilities/src/githost/git.ts: parsed git messages assume English where untranslated is not set; folders made before 29e0c81 keep the machine's autocrlf.

packages/runtime/src/daemon/task-words.ts's merge-state branch and the merge-side sentences (merge.ts, pr-executor.ts emptiedSentence, pull-requests.ts rows): labels and sentences read a subset of the merge record (any last_outcome but 'conflict' reads 'waiting for you to merge'; the waiting_checks sentence whatever the status) and offer ways out no button gives.

decisions: W15-12: a tool output whose shape cannot be confirmed and that holds a resolved secret is denied with a reason and an audit row; never pass a resolved secret. The SDK ships the shapes as TypeScript types only (sdk-tools.d.ts), so conformance is checked with one typed fixture per allowed built-in tool, which pnpm typecheck re-checks on every SDK upgrade.

W15-13: one rule for the write cap and the cut-off retry: a call is paid only from the money below the run's wrap-up line (as web search already is); the raised cap applies to the retried call only; complete tool_use blocks of a cut reply may be kept (U-085 amendment) if it stays safe (a cut block is never run).

W15-15/W15-17: the web search offer is decided once at the run's start (affordable or not, with the loop's own arithmetic) and its definition stays byte-identical while it is offered; the limits stay in code: max_uses fixed at the start, its full worst case counted on every call that offers it, and the tool dropped once (one cache rewrite) at the first call where the searches left or the money below the line no longer cover it; never 'told in text' instead (ADR 0107's 'a search never eats the reserve' holds).

W15-14/W15-16: 'Left to do' counts only what the criteria still need; the wrap-up's log line and its model-facing text say what is really true (ADR 0112 amendment), and their amounts under a centime read 'less than CHF 0.01'.
W15-18: estimates get a deterministic size factor from the outcome and criteria; the plan card and the Start dialog keep showing the same figure (R-estimates).
W15-20: actual_cost_usd_micro stays the work-only budget counter; a separate ledger-based 'spent' figure is what the person reads.
W15-21: per-call booking on the task and the Run row is atomic; a person's action during a run must not fail on the version bump.

W15-59, W15-69, W15-70: w15-run adds the session outcome's fields (the tasks the person cancelled, a paused count, waitingPrs split into checks pending and GitHub not answering) to runner.ts and session.ended, and writes their sentences in session/result.ts and event-lines.ts endedCounts.
root_causes: packages/runtime/src/agent/loop.ts: per-call sizing (write room, cut-off floor, max_uses) is recomputed each call from rules that contradict each other and ignore the wrap-up line or the prompt cache.

packages/runtime/src/session/budget-pause.ts and executor.ts: the handoff parser and the pause rule treat any listed line as unfinished work; the wrap-up words describe a spend threshold while the code triggers on spend plus the next call's worst case; amounts are formatted without moneyWords.
packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts searchPlanFor: the brief's search line is decided without the money the loop checks.
packages/runtime/src/estimates/model.ts: estimates know only specialist and tier; a killed run is taken as a sample.

packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts and executor.ts: spend reaches the task and the Run row only when the run returns, and reviews never reach the task's figure; the session outcome has no cancelled tasks, no paused count and one waitingPrs count, so session/result.ts and event-lines.ts endedCounts cannot say what happened.

W15-14 (budget-pause.test.ts and real-daemon with the stand-in researcher at Budget 0.15): a run that hears the wrap-up and lists only 'Nothing for the acceptance criteria.' and an 'Optionally …' extra is reviewed and Done; no 'paused at its budget' card; parseHandoff on the live report returns no blocking items; the wrap-up request text asks for criteria-only items or 'nothing'.

W15-15 (loop-web-search.test.ts with PromptCacheSim taught the API's web-search/max_uses rules; a stand-in model that searches on every call): every request of one run that offers web_search sends a byte-identical web_search definition (max_uses and lists fixed at the run's start); the tool is dropped at most once in the run and never re-added; each call's cache_read >= the previous call's cache_read + cache_creation except at that one drop; the run's searches never exceed the task's searches left (ten over all its runs); every call that offers the tool counts the full max_uses in its pre-call worst case; no search is paid from the reserve kept to finish (spend when the wrap-up is told <= the run's line; the tool is gone from that call on); no limit relies on text alone.

W15-27: TR-15 as ADR 0112's amendment of 2026-11-09 designs it; a changed head or attempt falls back to today's rerun.
W15-28: the runtime decides between a questions card and a sign-off before the critic files anything.

W15-33: the plan card's 'reads no website' line is one function in plan-tasks.ts beside cannotRunHere, in a field the card already renders.

root_causes: packages/runtime/src/loop/try-plan.ts: a prose command ends at a stop word with no arguments and is run bare; expectsError reads only its own sentence.

packages/runtime/src/loop/critic.ts: the review's evidence is built from the task's title and outcome and the last run's result only (no site rule, no earlier runs' pages); the sign-off is filed before the runtime decides the card.
packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts / budget-card.ts: a refused review keeps no result, so the next session reruns the specialist.
packages/runtime/src/brief.ts, session/executor.ts, capabilities/src/web/fetch.ts: no date and no read time anywhere a specialist or the critic looks.
evals/registry/specialists/*/specialist.md: an unconditional default output file; packages/runtime/src/session/intake.ts: the empty-list rule says what not to plan, never what to plan instead.

The words of reviews and tries: the sent-back line built from the summary's first 100 characters, ruledSummary's dead branches, a raw verdict in the Critic column, Playwright's exception text, a package.json that is not there, markdown tables and one row per read in the drawer.

One commit per item: the failing test first at the person's boundary named in its acceptance line (a real-daemon case, a composed daemon test, a UI test, or the unit test of the function that writes the sentence), then the fix, then the siblings (validation rule 8; log what you find in new_problems). problems: [fix] W15B-01 (major, data loss): a resume or a redo from main of a branch whose pull request is open (the Tasks-row Redo of a done task, with or without a merge card; a Try again) resets the task's folder and drops a commit the person made there without a word; Evidence: wave15a-review-w15-merge:non_blocking[6], wave15a-fixup-w15-merge:not_done[1] and new_problems[1], wave15a-merge:problems_left[1] (4); Root cause at 3600089: packages/capabilities/src/githost/pr-executor.ts executeIn resets at two sites without asking folderHold (:277-310; callers only :2000 and merge.ts:1930): (1) the resume with no work in progress, :1011 createBranch(branch, origin/branch); (2) the redo from main (a Redo with an open merge card closes it with REDO_FROM_BASE, commands/task.ts:308-322; conflictAnswer reads 'dropped', :2834): the branch keeps its name while its PR is open (:968) and :1087 createBranch(branch, depsBase ?? origin/base) runs checkout -B (git.ts:496) over it. :922 cleanAfterCutShortRun sets uncommitted changes aside under failedRef (kept, silently).

decisions: W15B-01: hold, never reset and never bring the person's commit along unasked (as W15-02's rebuild; ADR 0111). Before the reset at :1011, and before the one at :1087 when the branch keeps its name because its PR is open, folderHold 'commits' ends the run before any model call: nothing reset, no spend; executeIn returns { outcome: 'needs_human', summary: <sentence>, costUsdMicro: 0, branch } as its dependency-base refusal does (:1039, :1079). The runner (unchanged) sets the task needs_human with that reason and files the cannot-run card ('"X" could not run. <sentence>', Try again / Cancel task); the row reads 'Needs your decision: it could not run' and offers Answer, Edit, Cancel. So the sentence names Try again, never Redo: resume 'Its task folder has a commit that is not on GitHub: push it or undo it, then press Try again.'; redo from main 'Its task folder has a commit that is not on GitHub, and doing the task again from main would drop it: undo it or keep it on another branch, then press Try again.'. The session goes on with other tasks. The sentence reaches the row, the card and the session log only as the run's summary: no edit to task-words.ts, task-display.ts, event-lines.ts or runner.ts (w15-words' W15B-79 makes the log's task.finished line say the run's sentence). Not built in run B: an immediate answer at the Redo itself (commands/task.ts task.reopen with a folder port; a hint for run C, where D6 changes what Redo does). Uncommitted changes stay as built (set aside under failedRef, kept) unless the executor can tell cheaply that the last run finished; the report says which. Tasks-row actions still start no work (D6 is run C's). The owner is asked to confirm hold (new owner question).

W15B-02: the safety part only (W5-40 stays open). One guard where every start passes: compose.ts startSession (:3300) refuses an archived project with one sentence ('The project "<name>" was removed, so nothing of it runs.' or the fixer's §5 words), which covers POST /sessions, the chat's session.start, a credential wake, a budget resume, a plan approval's start and a handover job; POST /sessions refuses at once with the same sentence before requestStart (no session row); credentialWaits.wake skips a removed project and drops its wait (the next tick does not retry it); refreshJobSchedules schedules no handover for it; the intake's propose refuses it and its filing re-reads the status right before the insert, so a plan drafted during the Undo is never filed; the creation's Undo is refused while a session of that project runs ('Cannot be undone now: a session of <name> is running. Stop it first.'); ProjectPage reads the status GET /projects/:id already returns and says 'This project was removed.' with no Start session or Create a repository. No api-types or views.ts change. D6 (run C) removes the wake's own start; until then this guard stops it.

W15B-03: coverage, not a fix. One composed conversation test at the chat's boundary with a scripted chat model that obeys a questions card's quoted words: a card that orders a wider site rule, a task cancel and a budget raise ends the turn in the read-back with nothing changed, and the request's system text carries the data rule. Expected to pass at 3600089: committed as a guard, and the report says it passed at once (rule 8 is for fixes). If a code-enforced part fails, that is a real bug: the case stays failing first, the fix goes in the gate (packages/commands/src/executor.ts decideSteps, or a spec's narrows or limit flag in commands/settings.ts), siblings after. conversation/agent.ts is not edited in run B (run C's D3). A narrowing the card's words ask for acts at once by design; no code can tell it from the person's own: that is W15B-80, later for run C.
W15B-05: about 15 s of re-reads per poll in all, through the watcher's clock; stop() ends the wait; no GitHub call after stop.

W15B-07: PlanTaskView.note (append-only) with 'Reads no website: this project's "only these websites" list is empty. Add websites in Settings, or Change the plan.'; plan-tasks.ts reads the rule from deps.estimate.project.settings and a new PlanTasksDeps.readsWeb(name), passed at server.ts:1861-1871 from the registry; the fake daemon in the same commit; InboxPage renders it beside runsOn.
W15B-08: tests only; a failing case is a real bug, fixed in the same commit.

Not in this area (the owner's answers of 2026-11-09 give them to run C): W15B-04 (the Docs note while another project's status PR is open; D1), W15B-06 (the chat reads the status kept in the app; D3), W15B-09 (a project named only as a word in the chat's card selection; D3) and W15B-80 (a narrowing a card's words ask for; D3).

status 'archived' is read only by Changes: nothing that starts work (a press, a wake, a schedule), files a plan or shows a project page knows a project was removed, and the creation's Undo does not ask whether its session runs.
The chat's card facts (W15-30) carry model text into a model that holds command tools, with a rule but no hostile test of the gate behind it.
The watcher's re-read was written per PR with a bare setTimeout, outside the clock stop() controls.
The plan card reads only per-install limitations; a per-project rule has no field, and its deps do not say who reads the web.
Run A left tests at internal seams where the binding rules ask for the person's boundary, the Inbox's options and a restart.

triage.item: Status pull request: a project writes into another project's open status PR on the shared fr/status branch and lists it with Merge
triage.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live2-result.json github F2; daemon.log 04:49:57 'status update written ... branch fr/status ... pull/5'; git diff 6759c4b..152f5ac on origin/fr/status in /tmp/frbench/live2/github/work/sandbox; /tmp/frbench/live2/github/github-a/steps/160-c57-status-p2-overview.txt
triage.note: Model not involved. The setting stays off by default (C-57). Builds only the safety part until the owner answers W15-112: the status and scaffold PR bodies carry a hidden ownership marker (the project's id, one form shared with W15-08); a project never pushes to, comments on or lists another project's status or scaffold PR; while another project's status PR is open on fr/status, this project writes no status PR (its status stays in the app, docs/status.md in its copy as today, and one log line says why); with none open, today's behaviour (fr/status, one PR). A legacy fr/status PR without a marker counts as this project's only when no other project on this install is linked to the repository; with two linked, neither writes to it or lists it. No per-project status branch and no second PR: both would change one docs/status.md and conflict on merge, which is the owner's question (W15-112). Amend ADR 0106 points 3 and 5. Root cause at 931ed52: Holds at 931ed52: packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:100 STATUS_BRANCH = 'fr/status' (one name for every project); docs.ts:800-826 writeSessionStatus starts from the open PR's branch, pushes without force and comments on it (:812, :815); docs.ts:970-973 checkout takes the first open PR by head only; docs.ts:146 isProjectDocsPr counts any fr/status PR as this project's when the setting is on; the status PR body names no project (no scaffoldProjectLine). Sibling: docs.ts:729-746 the scaffold still pushes to and comments on another project's open fr/docs-scaffold PR when it writes files. Check revision: ["decision narrowed to the safety part (adversarial check spec_problems[0]): the earlier per-project branch fr/status-<project> and 'B has its own status PR' pre-empted owner question W15-112 and made two PRs on one docs/status.md"]

triage.item: Changing the web search offer mid-run (max_uses down, or the tool dropped) voids the prompt cache: a quarter to a third of a research run's cost is cache rewrites
triage.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live2-result.json research F3; model-calls-final.jsonl seq 9-10 (read 0, wrote 46,770) and seq 31-34
triage.note: Keep the web_search definition (max_uses and the domain lists) byte-identical for the run while it stays affordable, and keep every limit in code: max_uses is fixed once at the run's start from the smaller of the task's searches left (ten over all its runs) and what the money below the run's wrap-up line pays; every call that offers the tool counts the full max_uses in its pre-call worst case; at the first call where the searches left or the money below the line no longer cover it (or the wrap-up was told), the tool is dropped for the rest of the run and never re-added: one cache rewrite, once, instead of one per call. No limit relies on text: a server tool is billed whatever the text says, and ADR 0107's guarantee that a search never eats the reserve kept to finish (fixup-web-search B1, ADR 0112 amendment) holds. Teach PromptCacheSim the API's web-search/max_uses invalidation. Amend ADR 0107 point 9 and the ADR 0112 note on fewer searches near the line. Avoidable waste per run is about USD 0.07-0.11. Root cause at 931ed52: Holds at 931ed52: packages/runtime/src/agent/loop.ts:563-583 recomputes maxUses every call from the money below the line; :632-643 leaves webSearch out when 0; packages/runtime/src/provider/anthropic.ts:280-282 appends the tool per call (its comment assumes the tools mark protects the cache); testenv/src/provider/prompt-cache.ts:96-131 ignores req.webSearch, so tests never see the rewrite. Check revision: ["decision corrected (adversarial check spec_problems: 'enforced in the estimate and in text, never by editing the tools' dropped the code limit of ADR 0107/0112; verified at loop.ts:555-583 and ADR 0107 web-search point 4)"]

wave7_live_check_after_merge: After the whole wave is merged, the full suite is green, CI is green on Windows and Linux and the Desktop app workflow ran, the session lead walks six journeys with the real model (details and pass criteria: /tmp/frbench/phaseE7-live.md). Cap USD 4.00 in total, stopping at a clean point; GitHub only on joelwellbournewood/forerunner-sandbox; nothing printed or committed of any key. (1) Merging, about USD 1.10, bench-live: a 3-task chain left at 'You press Merge' (Overview, the dependents' words, Open this version, Merge in order as merge commits, Files within a minute without a session, Take this work out naming the dependent), then a 2-task chain whose first PR is squash-merged on GitHub's website (the dependent rebuilt, only its own commits, merges cleanly), then 'Merge automatically after review' with one task. (2) Credentials, about USD 0.20, on the routed provider (no --provider flag; bench-live ignores the vault): an invalid key in the bench's vault gives one 'Anthropic refused your API key' card and a waiting task; saving the real key starts it by itself; a research plan card says where it runs and why. (3) Budgets, about USD 0.90, bench-live: a coder task whose budget is about three times the reserve its run's log names hears the wrap-up, pauses with a local commit, and Continue finishes it with one review; a tiny budget (CHF 0.02) pauses with the save only and no wrap-up text; Cancel on a paused task names the stuck dependent. (4) Research with web search, about USD 1.00, bench-live: the server tool with max_uses at most 10, blocks sent back unchanged, no 400 (a '*.' block-list entry included), sources only from opened pages, the cost well under 2026-11-02's USD 1.32; then 'Only these websites: developer.mozilla.org' refuses another site and the report names the rule. (5) Costs, about USD 0.40: smoke.cjs --live on a fresh bench, each kind within about x2 of the plan card's estimate, cache reads after the first call. (6) The window: the Desktop app workflow's window check on Windows with Ctrl+click on Inbox (no model cost). Reserve about USD 0.40 for one retry. The subscription-only items (Claude Code stopped at a budget stop and counted once; the page reader, the WebSearch lists and the wrapper on the subscription; the SDK refusal card) go to the owner's checklist step 6, with what to look for; the three owner questions go to the owner with the U-entries. Findings go to a fix round with the same pipeline; spend is added to NEXT-SESSION.md.

Wave 7 leaves room: fix/decisions' status_pull_request switch and the status PR stay as they are until wave 8 replaces them (the owner's 'status' decision supersedes that session-lead default; 'merge-in-app' lists the status PR as a docs PR that merges only on the person's click, and 'merged-copy''s lock covers its write); no wave 7 area removes the docs/status.md template ('No docs/status.md in repositories' is wave 8's); the merge record carries agent_id and the paused work is per install, and sharing them across installs or people is the collaboration module's.

Choosing the starting merge mode by reading the repository at linking (automatic checks, Pages or deployments from main): the owner chose 'you press Merge' as every project's default; the automatic mode's change card states the risk in words instead.
'Give this session CHF N more' between tasks (research option D) and raising a running task's budget (option E): not asked for; 'Continue (CHF N more)' starts the next session at once instead.
Anthropic's task budget (beta) and the Agent SDK's alpha taskBudget on the subscription: later, as a measured trial, only if tasks pass as often.
Web search's dynamic filtering (search run from code execution): later; the first version sends the tool without it.

Reading the home or office network, a global 'never these sites' list, robots.txt in Forerunner's reader (the owner was told the two readers differ there), and reading pages through a proxy (only the plain sentence is built).

Running Claude Code inside the Docker sandbox so the subscription can run commands: an untested idea; the chooser and the 'Code tasks that need commands' setting cover the gap for now, with the plan card saying when tests will not run.
Linking the person's own working copy of a repository: the owner said no ('own_folder'); the PC copy stays Forerunner's own under its data folder.

Stacked pull requests, holding a dependent task until its dependency is merged, and one pull request per session: rejected in the research (merge order on the person, the stall the owner met, a large rework).

Anthropic's terms question on storing a Claude.ai token for the Agent SDK: only Anthropic can settle it; the subscription reader is still built because the owner decided 'on both credentials', and web search is built on the API key first.
Live checks that need a Claude subscription token (no token in the cloud environment): the owner's checklist step 6.
The merge of wave 6 (stops, asking, decisions, verification with their fix-ups) and CI green on it: a precondition, not wave 7 work; every wave 7 fixer starts from that merge.

Three owner questions are not left out but built with a stated default and asked in their U-entries (AGENTS.md: a choice about what a person sees goes to the owner as options): what 'wait' means with a second credential ('credential-limits', U-078), whether commands become a hard need on projects with dependencies ('credential-chooser', U-078), and the 'Local only' copy back when the person changed a file during a run ('merged-copy', U-037). The session lead puts their answers into the areas before those areas merge, or the built default stands.

Review points narrowed or corrected, with the reason: (1) 'budget-stop''s pause rule: the review would pause a run whose 'Left to do:' list has items even without a wrap-up; built narrower (a wrap-up in this run and items left, or a budget stop), because a pause card would otherwise name a limit that was not reached. (2) 'credential-limits''s bench step: there is no `--provider none`; the routed provider runs with no --provider flag, and the bench gets `--provider bench-api` (the routed provider pointed at the stand-in, only in a repository checkout). (3) The no-replay marker: both of the review's options are built (the deps base with --no-ff, and the marker kept until the branch is rebuilt). (4) The size review's splits are taken (merge-record and dependent-branches, merged-copy and merged-actions, polish-desktop and polish), and 'credentials' is split too (credential-limits and credential-chooser), because with the review's additions it was the largest area; 'polish' keeps its key so handoffs.json['polish'] still reaches it. (5) The old planned group ['cost', 'polish'] is replaced by wave 7's groups, not kept beside them, so neither area runs twice. Nothing else in the review was rejected: every problem's evidence was read at the scratch merge 6488a14 and holds.
wave7_owner_questions: U-078: what 'When my first choice runs out mid-session: wait' means when a second credential could serve. Built: (a) nothing moves onto the other credential: the stopped task and the session's other tasks on that credential wait for its reset and start by themselves (owner-answers.md section 2's words: 'switching moves work from plan limits onto money'). Option for the owner: (b) only the stopped task waits while the others go on to the other credential, as today (ADR 0100 point 4), with the stopped task's start scheduled at the reset. Changing the answer changes one rule in the pick and the sentences, not the tests' structure.

U-078: should running commands become a hard need for code tasks on a project with dependencies to install? Without commands the project's checks are skipped (project-checks.ts:105-108), so under the default 'my first choice anyway' such a task on the subscription gets neither its own tests nor the project's. Built: the owner's default, with the plan card saying the tests will not run there. Options: (a) keep it; (b) commands become a hard need for such projects, which sends most code work to the API key (money); (c) a third value of the setting, 'the API key when the project has dependencies'.

U-037: when the person changed a file in 'Local only' while a run was using it, what does the copy back do? Built: (a) the person's file wins and the agent's version is kept beside it, with one sentence in the task's result (nothing is lost). Options for the owner: (b) the agent's version wins and the person's is kept beside it; (c) the folder is read-only for the person while a run uses it.
